subject: shotgun
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: shotgun, in the place of the game's models/v_shotgun.mdl, models/p_shotgun.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, A, A, A where the asset was C, B, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief asks for a pump-action combat shotgun, a long gun with a straight stock. In the TOP and BELOW views (sides.png) the outline is an L: the barrel runs down and the stock turns about 90 degrees sideways at its end, about 17 units across. FRONT-LEFT and FRONT-RIGHT show the same elbow. The RIGHT view is straight, so the bend is in the top plane and is in the outline, not paint. The silhouette reads as a bent gun, not a shotgun.

M2.reason: The brief gives one size, about 30 long. The asset's long axis is 28.2, 6% short, well within 15%. Its 17.1 width comes from the stock bend and is not a size the brief asks for.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies: barrel, receiver, pump (forend), stock, trigger. The barrel, receiver and ribbed pump are there (the pump shows clearly in first-person.png). The stock is a hooked, bent piece in the top and below views, not the straight stock a pump shotgun has, so it is the wrong shape. A trigger is not distinguishable in any view. A part the brief names is wrong in shape, so M3 is at most 1.

M4.reason: The brief asks for black metal with a wooden or dark pump and stock. The asset's metal is dark grey-black with lighter highlights, and its pump and stock are dark. The brief allows a dark pump and stock, so the colours and materials agree with it. No ΔE measure is given for a brief leg, so this is by eye.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings, lettering or stripes. The asset has ribbed grooves on the receiver and pump and no added marks; nothing it adds is wrong against the brief.

M6.reason: The line-up test (lineup.png, four readings) caught the asset once in four askings: the judges picked D, A, A, A where the asset stood at C, B, A, C. That is under the two-catch line, so the line-up does not cap it. The M6 score is capped at 2 for this leg as the judge's instructions state.

M7.reason: The muzzle points forward (small tip at the left end of the right view) and the stock is at the back. In the side views it lies flat on its side as a world weapon does. Its origin could not be checked beyond that, and no fault shows.

M8.reason: The checks report no errors. The asset has 174 triangles, under the bar for its kind: the Half-Life median is 138, and the bar is the larger of twice the median (276) and the three-quarter mark (187). Nothing open is visible in the views; the muzzle ring in FRONT is a bore the game also shows.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits in the orange glove where the game's own shotgun sits (right of the picture), held the same way, the same way round, with the muzzle up-left. In attack.png the gun stays on the glove through the SHOOT frames (0/20 to 20/20) and traces the recoil arc with the hand. The frames are cropped at the bottom so the contact is seen only in part. Note: the two first-person pictures look almost identical, so the asset's v_ model may be close to Valve's own shotgun design; that is not scored here.
